records.rationale: Both added exports retain cgroup_taskset_first/next for the generic Android cgroup attach hooks, which hand modules a cgroup_taskset. Native iterator functions are byte-identical to LTS, including current subsystem-configuration guard and destination css choice. Taskset iteration uses the migration caller serialization and borrowed task/css pointers, not an independent refcounted snapshot. This is source-level GPL module customization, not historical binary KMI.

records.rationale: Retain all three GPL css_task_iter_start/next/end exports as a complete module iteration interface. Whole native functions match LTS. The iterator holds current task and css-set references under native css_set_lock; next releases the previous task, end is required even after early termination. A module must hold any separately retained task reference and valid starting CSS lifetime. Native synchronization remains, and this does not expose iteration as an unprivileged syscall.

records.rationale: Retain GPL cgroup_add_dfl_cftypes for generic Android vendor controller extensions on cgroup v2. Function and registration implementation are native LTS, including disabled-subsystem handling, default-only flag, mutex serialization and error cleanup. No new cgroup file is instantiated merely by exporting the function. Modules adding controls must implement appropriate permissions/LSM policy and preserve callback/descriptor lifetime until removal; default cftype modes do not make arbitrary new module handlers safe.

records.rationale: Retain GPL cgroup_rm_cftypes as the teardown counterpart to exported registration helpers. Native removal body and locked removal path match LTS: unregister cftypes and remove kernfs files before callbacks/module storage can disappear. The module must unregister successfully before unload and obey registration serialization; the export alone does not automatically pin module callbacks or guarantee arbitrary module unload correctness. CONFIG_MODULE_UNLOAD=y makes this paired interface relevant to the selected configuration.

records.rationale: Read all three changed paths and retain four generic CPU-controller lifecycle notifications plus GPL cpu_cgrp_subsys export. sched_move_task notification precedes task_rq_lock and sees the pre-update scheduler group; native scoped sched_change guards, SCX move and conditional reschedule stay intact. Early allocation receives NULL parent for root, ordinary allocation is after successful sched_create_group and cannot replace errors. Adapt 97a12e6cd2f3: notify css_free BEFORE sched_unregister_group queues the final RCU free, preventing an already-reclaimed CSS from reaching a callback. Original post-unregister placement had no surrounding RCU read lock in css_free_rwork_fn; the tracepoint own later protection cannot retroactively protect it. This deliberately changes notification ordering relative to native fair/RT unregister; callbacks must finish vendor cleanup before teardown, accept already-released CSS, and never retain it or resurrect its dead refcount. Whole native teardown is preserved. Exact vendor callback policies remain unverified.

security: These exports retain native core implementations and permit trusted vendor module source customization. Registration APIs require descriptor/callback lifetime through successful removal and do not automatically keep arbitrary modules alive. Hook ordering fix preserves native RCU teardown and prevents notification after possible reclamation; it deliberately changes post-unregister observation to pre-unregister cleanup. No callback may acquire a new reference to the already-dead CSS.
uncertainty: No exact callback/registration consumer found in scoped manifest/common-modules or GrapheneOS system/core/frameworks/native search. This is not evidence of universal absence; retain generic Android vendor source interfaces conservatively under the compatibility priority. No actual module control registration, unload race, runtime migration, or boot verified.
validation: Whole native-body comparisons; 16 extracted-free-function scheduling models have zero invalid reads, versus seven for old code. Reclamation is modeled, not a reproduced kernel RCU race. Full build needed for 97a12e6cd2f3.

subsequent_build_verification.result: Full existing emulator workflow succeeded. 100 common and 45 virtual-device modules verified against exact build certificate, tampered payload rejected; 659 protected exports and all 145 module flag/CRC tables checked.
